HTTP Methods

You might say

AI said to use POST instead of GET here. What does that mean?

The verb in a request stating which kind of operation it performs: read, create, update, or delete·In the Network panel, GET /api/articles/7 and POST /api/articles are different requests. GET means safe reading; POST asks the target resource to process the request, and whether it creates or saves depends on the API contract. A method states request semantics; choosing the wrong one does not guarantee a 405 response.
Know first
HTTP
GET / POST
What operation each common method corresponds to
Network · GET /api/articles/7
MethodGET
Request bodyNone
ResponseArticle record
Read request returned

GET is for safe reading: repeating it does not change the server resource. Check separately whether the page shows the result you need.

Why method semantics matter

GET is read: Address-bar Enter and ordinary links are GET; it is designed to be safely resent and should have no side effects.

POST submits a request for processing: Forms commonly use POST, but POST does not inherently mean save or create; check the API contract for the operation it triggers.

PUT / DELETE update and remove: Express modification and deletion per the API contract; some APIs use POST uniformly for compatibility—follow the API docs.

What it does not tell you

A 405 response says the resource does not allow that method; it does not prove whether data changed. A method error may produce another status, so compare the response with the API contract.

The delete button currently sends a GET request, and refresh deletes again. Change it to the semantically correct method (DELETE or the API's agreed POST) and confirm refreshing does not re-trigger it. Verify the method and result in the Network panel afterward.
